page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn2ne.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 12 dedicated vCPUs on an Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor running at 2.5 GHz with an x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 48.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage, and offers a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates that the instance delivers average multi-core performance but exhibits weak single-core capabilities. In stress-ng and Geekbench testing, multi-core scores fall within the middle 50% tier, whereas single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3, rank in the bottom 10% to 25%. Memory bandwidth is moderate, with uncached read speeds of 56.47 GB/sec and write speeds of 44.31 GB/sec, though the overall Passmark memory score is weak.

Given its hardware profile, the ecs.sn2ne.3xlarge is suited for multi-threaded workloads that can leverage its 12 dedicated cores, such as software compilation, multi-threaded decompression, and moderate database operations. However, it is less optimal for single-threaded applications or high-throughput web serving. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the use of older Intel Xeon Broadwell architecture offers a stable, dedicated resource pool for general-purpose workloads at a lower resource-density cost compared to newer generation hardware, albeit with lower per-core performance.
